When the British and French both seized American vessels if they touched at the ports of the other, Jefferson decided to test `text(one)` of his favorite doctrines — that war was both intolerable and unnecessary, and that the best weapon against both powers lay in economic sanctions. He got Congress to pass a series of `text(five)` Embargo Acts, stringently forbidding U.S. trade with Britain and France not only overseas but even along the Canadian border. . . .
